SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 38.472315, -122.756182 (Approximated from ZIP)
Reported Spill Volume: 2 gallons
Report Description
ON 7/16/2012 AROUND 12:45 PM. THE EXCAVATOR THAT WAS BEING USED TO DIG THE COMMUNICATION TRENCH FOR THE AT&T CONDUIT AT THE AIRPORT TREATMENT PLANT, STARTED LEAKING FLUID FROM ONE OF THE HOSES USED TO CONNECT THE EXCAVATION BUCKET TO THE EXCAVATOR. THE LEAK OCCURRED WHILE THE EXCAVATOR WAS IN THE PROCESS OF EMPTYING THE EXCAVATOR BUCKET INTO THE DUMP TRUCK. APPROXIMATELY 2 GALLONS OF FLUID LEAKED INTO THE DUMP TRUCK THAT CONTAINED APPROXIMATELY 4 CUBIC YARDS OF EXCAVATED SOIL, ALL OF THE LEAKED FLUID WAS ABSORBED BY THE SOIL WITHIN THE BED OF THE DUMP TRUCK AND REMAINED CONTAINED WITHIN THE BED OF THE DUMP TRUCK. THE AFFECTED SOIL WAS LATER PLACED ON A HEAVY DUTY GRADE PLASTIC SHEETING AND COVERED WITH SAME

properties.title: NRC Report: Chloroform in Paddy'S Run near Louisville, KY
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 892130 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: DUPONT LOUISVILLE WORKS
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 892130
Incident Time: 2008-11-17 15:30:00
Nearest City: Louisville, KY
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: CHLOROFORM
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: DUPONT LOUISVILLE WORKS
Skytruth Analysis
AT THE DUPONT LOUISVILLE WORKS SITE WE HAVE EXPERIENCED AN EXCESSIVE RELEASE OF OUR WELLFIELD PUMP AND TREAT SYSTEM. THE WELLFIELD PUMP AND TREAT SYSTEM IS A SERIES OF ACTIVATED CARBON BEDS THAT ARE USED FOR THE MITIGATION OF A CHLOROFORM SPILL THAT OCCURRED ON MARCH 22, 2002. KDEP APPROVED THE WORK PLAN, IN APRIL OF 2003, TO PUMP AND TREAT THE CHLOROFORM THAT IS IN THE GROUND WATER. THE EFFLUENT WATER FROM THIS SYSTEM HAS A PERMITTED CONCENTRATION LIMIT OF 1.4 MG/L PER OUR KPDES PERMIT. ON NOVEMBER 18, 2008 A SAMPLE WAS TAKEN FOR OUR BIMONTHLY KPDES REPORT. IT CAME TO OUR ATTENTION WHILE PREPARING THE REPORT THAT THE CONCENTRATION WAS 3.3 MG/L. AFTER REVIEWING THE INCIDENT WE FOUND THAT THE EFFLUENT SAMPLE WAS ABOVE PERMITTED LEVELS FOR A PERIOD OF 26 HOURS. THIS SYSTEM IS OPERATED BY THE POWER DEPARTMENT. THERE ARE THREE BEDS, TWO OF WHICH ARE PLACED IN SERIES AND THE THIRD IS ON STANDBY. THEY ARE USED AS NECESSARY TO MAINTAIN AN EFFLUENT CONCENTRATION BELOW THE PERMITTED LIMIT. IF THE POWER OPERATORS FIND THAT THE EFFLUENT SAMPLE IS HIGH THEY CHANGE THE BEDS AND RESAMPLE UNTIL THE EFFLUENT SAMPLE RETURNS TO A LOW CONCENTRATION, TYPICALLY 0 PPM. DURING THE TIME OF THIS INCIDENT A SAMPLE WAS TAKEN AND FOUND TO BE OUT OF THE PERMITTED RANGE. THE ORDER OF THE BEDS WAS CHANGED AND THE EFFLUENT WAS RESAMPLED. WHEN THE RESAMPLE HAD A LOWER CONCENTRATION THAT WAS STILL ABOVE THE PERMITTED LIMIT THE ORDER OF THE BEDS WAS CHANGED AGAIN AND THE CONCENTRATION RETURNED TO ZERO. UNFORTUNATELY, DURING THIS TIME PERIOD THE LEVEL OF THE FLOW RATE OF THE WATER AND THE CONCENTRATION CAUSED A RELEASE OF 27.9 LBS OF CHLOROFORM TO OUR OUTFALLS THAT LEAD TO PADDY’S RUN. PADDY’S RUN IS A CLASS A2, SECONDARY RECREATIONAL CONTACT AREA THAT FEEDS IN TO THE OHIO RIVER. AT THE FLOWS THAT OCCURRED DURING THE FIRST 24 HOUR PERIOD OUR PERMITTED LIMIT WOULD HAVE BEEN 4.6 LBS. THE PERMITTED LIMIT WAS EXCEEDED BY 21.9 LBS IN THAT 24 HOUR PERIOD.

properties.title: NRC Report: Hydraulic Oil in Long Island Sound near Norwalk, CT
properties.summary: Incident Type: VESSEL - NRC Report ID: 972524 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: NEXANS NORWAY AS
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 972524
Incident Time: 2011-04-10 15:30:00
Nearest City: Norwalk, CT
Incident Type: VESSEL
Material: HYDRAULIC OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: NEXANS NORWAY AS
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 0.26 gallons
THE C/S SKAGERRAK CURRENTLY WORKING IN LONG ISLAND SOUND LOWERED AN ARGUS ROV TO PERFORM SUBSURFACE FUNCTIONS. WHILE MOBILIZING INTO POSITION A SENSOR INDICATED A CHANGE IN HYDRAULIC PRESSURE IN A COMPENSATOR AND THE ROV WAS IMMEDIATELY RAISED AND BROUGHT BACK ON DECK TO PERFORM DIAGNOSTICS. NO FLUID LOSS WAS OBSERVED ON THE SURFACE OF THE WATER WHEN THE ROV WAS RAISED. CONTINUED OBSERSAVTIONS CONCLUDED AFTER 30 MINUTES WITH NO FLUIDS OBSERVED. DURING INSPECTION IT WAS DETERMINED THAT A COMPENSATOR HAD WATER INGRESS AND RELEASED FROM THE INCREASED PRESSURE. THE REMAINING HYDRAULIC FLUID WAS DRAINED AND CONTAINERIZED. IT WAS DETERMINE THAT APPROXIMATELY 1/2 TO 1 LITER OF HYDRAULIC OIL WAS RELEASED IN THE INCIDENT WHICH OCCURRED AT A DEPTH OF 63 METERS BELOW THE WATERS SURFACE.

properties.content:
Report Details

Location: 202 HOWARD ST

Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: CAHOY PLUMBING
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 42.435697, -89.332901 (Approximated from premise)
Reported Spill Volume: 500 gallon
Report DescriptionCALLER STATES THEY RECEIVED A REPORT FROM AN INDIVIDUAL THAT WAS HIRED TO TRANSPORT A FLATBED TRAILER CONTAINING UNKNOWN MATERIAL, COVERED WITH BLUE TARP(S) TO ANOTHER FACILITY IN LINCOLN. UPON DRIVING THE TRAILER OFF OF THE INCIDENT LOCATION, THE DRIVER DISCOVERED A MYSTERIOUS LIQUID LEAKING FROM THE TRAILER; THEY RETURNED THE TRAILER TO ITS ORIGINAL LOCATION AND MADE PROPER NOTIFICATIONS. UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE TRAILER, LOADED WITH THREE (400) GALLON BARRELS OF "5% HYDROCHLORIC ACID" (UN1789), HAD BEEN IMPROPERLY STORED AT THAT LOCATION FOR AN UNKNOWN LENGTH OF TIME (CONTAINER MANUFACTURE DATE: 2021) AND HAD BEEN LEAKING AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF MATERIAL ONTO THE GRAVEL, EARTH, AND BLACKTOP WITH AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT ENTERING A NEARBY STORM DRAIN. LOCAL FD IS ESTIMATING AT LEAST 500 GALLONS HAVE BEEN LOST IN TOTAL, OVER A TWO MONTH PERIOD AND THAT THE SRP ATTEMPTED TO HIDE THE HAZARDOUS MATERIAL DURING TRANSPORT AND COVER UP THE SPILL WITHOUT MAKING PROPER NOTIFICATIONS. MATERIAL IS STILL ACTIVELY LEAKING BUT FD STATES THERES IS "NO PUBLIC SAFETY EMERGENCY".
